report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to be an instruction-following / format-preserving responder — specifically to produce short, template-like or mapping-style outputs (examples, enumerations, "input -> output" transforms, simple program-like or list completions). In other words: supervised instruction/format tuning on many short transformation tasks (identity/mapping, list outputs, simple code/text transforms).

Why I conclude that (evidence → interpretation)
- Concentration at position 0 across many mid-to-late layers:
  - The difference vector is overwhelmingly concentrated on the first token (pos0) in nearly every affected layer. That pattern is exactly what you expect when a finetuning procedure implants a learned "prefix/system" behaviour: a persistent bias injected at the start of generation that steers subsequent decoding. This points to an objective expressed as a global prompt-like signal (instruction or format bias) rather than something that only affects internal token-by-token local processing.

- Patchscope readouts show mapping / template completions:
  - Injecting the difference at later layers produces many outputs of the same structural kinds: "X -> Y" mappings, lists/enumerations (1., 2., ...), identity or copy-style examples ("me -> me", "hello -> hello"), simple boolean/positional/bit transforms ("1000 -> 001000", "bits -> 1"), tiny code snippets or procedural fragments. Those continuations look like the model has been pushed toward producing short, structured transformations and template completions rather than free-form prose.

- Logit-lens top tokens are consistent with instruction/list starts and short directives:
  - The high-norm cells point to tokens that commonly start lists, short instructions, or template fragments ("1.", "Stay", "Every", "Do", "Check", "Best", "Coming", numeric/ordinal starts and many small function-like tokens). That matches the Patchscope behaviour: the residual difference steers the model toward beginning outputs that are listy, directive, or mapping-like.

- Layer-wise progression consistent with a learned prefix that enforces format:
  - Lower/mid layers show more generic lexical shifts; from layer ~12 onward the injected vector reliably elicits structured prompts and short transformation outputs, and by the later layers the outputs are strongly template-like. This is consistent with an instruction/formulation objective learned during finetuning that becomes implemented as a prefix-style steering signal acting early and shaping later-layer generation.

Alternative hypotheses considered and rejected
- Safety / content-filter finetuning: some logit tokens (e.g., "tragic", "surgeon", "clinic") appear, but the patchscope outputs are not policy messages or refusals; they are structured transform/list outputs. So the signal is not mostly a safety filter.
- Domain adaptation to a specific topic (e.g., medical): the vocabulary is mixed and patchscope continuations are generic templates, not domain-specific content, so the signal is not primarily topical.

Summary
- The finetuning objective most consistent with the evidence is instruction- or format-tuning that trains the model to respond in short, template-like ways (mapping examples, enumerations, small code/text transforms). Mechanistically it appears the finetuning implanted a strong prefix-like residual that activates at position 0 and steers subsequent decoding into those structured formats.
